Fungal infection.description: A fungal infection occurs when a fungus invades body tissue. Common types include ringworm, athlete's foot, and nail infections.

Allergy.description: An allergy is an immune system response to a foreign substance that is typically harmless to most people.

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is a chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus.
precautions: Do not lie down after eating

Chronic cholestasis.description: A condition where bile flow from the liver is reduced or blocked, causing bile to build up in the liver.

Drug Reaction.description: An adverse drug reaction is an undesired harmful effect resulting from the use of a medication.
precautions: Carry a list of drug allergies

Peptic ulcer disease.description: Open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach and the upper part of the small intestine.

AIDS.description: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is a chronic, life-threatening condition caused by the HIV virus.

Diabetes.description: A metabolic disease that causes high blood sugar due to insufficient insulin production or ineffective insulin use.

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically resulting in vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal cramps.

Bronchial Asthma.description: A condition where airways narrow, swell, and produce extra mucus, making breathing difficult.

Hypertension.description: High blood pressure is a common condition where the long-term force of blood against artery walls is high enough to cause health problems.

Migraine.description: A neurological condition characterized by intense, debilitating headaches often accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light.

Cervical spondylosis.description: Age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in the neck, causing neck pain and stiffness.

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).description: Loss of muscle function due to bleeding in the brain which damages nerve cells.

Jaundice.description: A condition causing yellowing of the skin and eyes due to excess bilirubin in the blood.

Malaria.description: A serious disease caused by parasites transmitted through mosquito bites, causing fever and chills.

Chicken pox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy blister-like rash on the skin.

Dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral disease causing high fever, severe headache, and joint pain.

Typhoid.description: A bacterial infection that spreads through contaminated food and water, causing high fever and abdominal pain.

Hepatitis A.description: A highly contagious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis A virus, spread through contaminated food and water.

Hepatitis B.description: A liver infection caused by the Hepatitis B virus, spread through blood and body fluids.

Hepatitis C.description: A viral infection that causes liver inflammation, transmitted primarily through blood contact.

Hepatitis D.description: A liver infection only occurring in people infected with Hepatitis B, often causing more severe disease.

Hepatitis E.description: A liver disease caused by the Hepatitis E virus, usually spread through contaminated drinking water.

Alcoholic hepatitis.description: Liver inflammation caused by excessive alcohol consumption over time.

Tuberculosis.description: A serious bacterial infection that mainly affects the lungs and can spread through airborne droplets.

Common Cold.description: A viral infection of the upper respiratory tract causing runny nose, sore throat, and mild fever.

Pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid.

Dimorphic hemorrhoids (piles).description: Swollen veins in the lowest part of the rectum and anus causing discomfort and bleeding.

Heart attack.description: Occurs when blood flow to part of the heart is blocked, causing damage to heart muscle.

Varicose veins.description: Enlarged, twisted veins usually appearing on the legs due to faulty valves allowing blood to pool.

Hypothyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone, slowing bodily functions.

Hyperthyroidism.description: A condition where the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone, accelerating metabolism.

Hypoglycemia.description: A condition where blood sugar levels drop below normal, causing shakiness, confusion, and weakness.

Osteoarthritis.description: A degenerative joint disease that occurs when the protective cartilage on the ends of bones wears down.

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of one or more joints causing pain and stiffness that can worsen with age.

(Vertigo) Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo.description: A sudden sensation that you are spinning, caused by calcium crystals dislodging in the inner ear.

Acne.description: A skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells.
precautions: Consult a dermatologist for severe cases

Urinary tract infection.description: An infection in any part of the urinary system, usually caused by bacteria entering the urethra.

Psoriasis.description: A chronic skin disease causing cells to build up rapidly on the skin surface, forming scales and red patches.
precautions: Follow prescribed topical or systemic treatment

Impetigo.description: A highly contagious bacterial skin infection causing red sores that rupture and crust over.
precautions: Do not share towels or clothing
